sourceSpan.excerpt: I I do feel so attracted by the kind of these ideas that there is a kind of overly scientific understanding of the world that we need a more holistic more spiritual understanding. We can't just reduce everything to a purely scientistic uh reductionist explanation of things. I'm so sympathetic to that. I think Elizabeth puts it so kind of so well and so forcefully. I just find myself unable to be persuaded by it but it's been very useful to uh I guess think about where my kind of proximate feeling about reality and my subjective feelings about reality ends and where my feeling that I just have to defer to something that feels deeply unintuitive and in some ways unpleasant.

missingCandidates.proposition: Marriott finds Oldfield's critique of scientistic reduction deeply attractive and forceful but remains unpersuaded because he believes he must defer where subjective appreciation ends to an unintuitive and potentially unpleasant account of reality.
missingCandidates.rationale: This is Marriott's requested final reflection and a major concession-plus-reaffirmation. Omitting it leaves the guests' closing exchange incompletely represented.
